articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions involving Iran, reflecting ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy towards the country.
Further details regarding the scope and specific changes of this amended general license are available on the Treasury Department's website.

body: On October 28, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities and threats posed by these regimes, aligning with U.S. foreign policy objectives.
The specific individuals and entities designated, along with the reasons for their inclusion, are detailed in the official announcement.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Reaches Settlement Agreement with OFAC
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has reached a settlement agreement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) on October 27, 2026.
The settlement addresses apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations, underscoring the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally.
The terms of the settlement and the nature of the alleged violations are outlined in the public release by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Frequently Asked Questions on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These updates provide further guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under U.S. sanctions programs.
The revised FAQs aim to clarify compliance requirements and assist in navigating complex sanctions scenarios.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain entities from Belarus and North Korea sanctions lists.
Additionally, OFAC issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance.
These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions, balancing enforcement with humanitarian considerations and evolving geopolitical landscapes.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses, providing specific authorizations related to the new measures.
The PAIPA aims to combat intellectual property theft and protect U.S. economic interests by targeting individuals and entities involved in such illicit activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: On October 16, 2026, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question.
This amendment extends the authorization period for transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela, originally set to expire on October 23, 2026, until April 21, 2027.
The updated guidance aims to facilitate humanitarian aid and support for the Venezuelan people in the aftermath of natural disasters.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related and Cuba Designations, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation on October 15, 2026.
These actions target individuals and entities involved in Iran's international financial networks and shadow banking activities, as well as a Cuban state-owned bank.
Concurrently, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions to provide guidance on these updated sanctions measures.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Individual from Venezuela-Related Sanctions List
body: On October 14, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of Jorge Jesús Rodríguez Gómez from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under the Venezuela sanctions program.
This delisting is part of a broader diplomatic effort and reflects Washington's recognition of the interim Venezuelan government.
Such removals can signal shifts in U.S. foreign policy and engagement with sanctioned countries.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations on October 13, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist activities globally.
The action was undertaken in coordination with multiple U.S. law enforcement agencies and Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit, highlighting international cooperation in combating these threats.

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Settles with OFAC for $11,662,930
body: Bank of America, N.A. has reached an $11,662,930 settlement with the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) on October 13, 2026.
The settlement addresses 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs, including those targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

These violations occurred due to issues such as channeling correspondent banking payments through blocked banks, allowing designated individuals to make payments, and failing to update watchlists promptly.

articles.headline: OCC Announces October 2026 Enforcement Actions Against Banks and Individuals
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, targeting both financial institutions and institution-affiliated parties (IAPs).
Actions against banks include a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program.

Additionally, the OCC imposed a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A., for similar BSA compliance failures, and issued Orders of Prohibition against two individuals for embezzling customer funds.

articles.headline: OCC Imposes Record $750 Million Penalty on Bank of America for BSA/AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a historic $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A., on October 13, 2026, for widespread breakdowns in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

This penalty, the largest in OCC history, stems from the bank's deficient transaction monitoring system, which failed to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and resulted in numerous late suspicious activity reports (SARs).

The OCC found that Bank of America knew for years about its failure to escalate potentially suspicious activities but did not correct this serious violation, despite a December 2024 cease-and-desist order requiring it to address its BSA/AML deficiencies.

articles.headline: DHS Updates Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List
body: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), as Chair of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), announced an update to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, effective October 29, 2026.

This update adds three entities to the list under Section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii) of the UFLPA, identifying them as working with the government of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor, or receive forced labor or members of persecuted groups out of Xinjiang.

The newly added entities are Baoding LYSZD Trade And Business Co., Ltd., Hetian Haolin Hair Accessories Co. Ltd. (and its aliases), and Hetian Taida Apparel Co., Ltd (and its alias), all involved in mining, producing, or manufacturing goods with forced labor in Xinjiang.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
